parts.text: In this experiment, you will determine the resistance per unit length of wire X . The circuit has been set up for you.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Carry out the following instructions, referring to Fig. 2.1. • Connect the crocodile clip C to the free end of the resistance wire. • Switch on. Adjust the position of the crocodile clip C until the current shown on the ammeter is as near to 0.40 A as possible. • Measure, and record in Table 2.1, the potential difference (p.d.) V across wire X . Switch off. • Repeat the procedure for I = 0.50 A, 0.60 A, 0.70 A and 0.80 A. Table 2.1 I / A V / V 0.40 0.50 0.60 0.70 0.80 [2]

ms.label: 2(a)
ms.text:
V values all increasing
V all < 3.00 V and to at least 1 dp

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Plot a graph of V / V ( y -axis) against I / A ( x -axis). [4]

graph:

parts.text: (c) (i) Determine the gradient G of the graph. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. G = ......................................................... [1]

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Calculate the resistance R of each centimetre of wire X , using the equation R = G × k l , where k = 1.0 Ω cm. Give the value for R , to a suitable number of significant figures for this experiment. R = ......................................................... [2]
